_comment: Severity rubric. There are no points and nothing is added up. 'findings' maps each check label to its possible outcomes, and each outcome to [severity, text]. Severities: critical = broken or unsupported today; high = an important protection is missing or weak; medium = an expected practice is missing; low = a refinement; info = optional, or could not be determined (listed, never counted); pass = the practice is met. audit_checks.assess_results() decides WHICH outcome applies; this file decides how serious it is and how it reads. An outcome that is not listed produces no finding. One cause, one finding: HSTS, DNSSEC and clickjacking protection are each a single check. End-of-life findings carry a dynamic label ('EOL OS: ubuntu 18.04') and take their severity from 'eol_severity'.

null_sender: SPF declares that the domain sends no mail (v=spf1 -all)
softfail: SPF soft fail only (~all) — not fully enforcing
no_all_mechanism: SPF record has no 'all' mechanism — no enforcement
redirect_no_all: SPF redirect target has no 'all' mechanism — no enforcement
redirect_target_no_spf: SPF redirect target has no SPF record (broken redirect)
pass_all_DANGEROUS: SPF ends in +all — every server on the internet is authorised to send as this domain
missing: SPF not published — any server can send mail as this domain
missing_covered: No SPF on this subdomain, which sends no mail — spoofing is covered by the parent domain's DMARC policy

exceeds_limit: SPF needs more than 10 DNS lookups — receivers treat the record as broken (RFC 7208)

quarantine: DMARC policy: quarantine — not yet at reject
none: DMARC policy p=none — monitoring only, not enforced
missing: DMARC not published — domain can be spoofed

none: DMARC sp=none — subdomains are not protected

missing: DMARC rua= aggregate reporting not configured

clean: MX targets are hostnames (not IP literals) and resolve directly to A/AAAA (no CNAME) (RFC 2181 §10.3)
cname_target: At least one MX target is a CNAME (RFC 2181 §10.3 violation — some receivers may bounce)
ip_literal: At least one MX target is an IP literal (RFC 5321 §5.1 violation — MX RDATA must be a hostname)
cname_and_ip: MX targets include both an IP literal and a CNAME target (RFC 2181 §10.3 / RFC 5321 §5.1 violations)

published: MTA-STS record published (the policy file could not be read from this audit)
none: MTA-STS policy mode is none — nothing is enforced
missing: MTA-STS policy not published — sending servers have no policy preventing fallback to plaintext
policy_broken: MTA-STS record published but the policy file is missing or unusable — sending servers ignore it

some_mx: DANE/TLSA on some but not all MX hosts
no_mx: No DANE/TLSA records on MX hosts (optional; needs DNSSEC)

tls_1_2: STARTTLS on MX negotiates TLS 1.2 (TLS 1.3 not offered)
no_starttls: STARTTLS not offered on at least one MX host — mail can travel in plaintext
unprobed: STARTTLS on MX could not be probed (port 25 likely blocked)

found: DKIM key found at common selector(s)
not_found: DKIM key not found at common selectors (the domain may use a custom selector)

good: DKIM key strength acceptable (Ed25519 or RSA ≥2048)
weak: DKIM key uses RSA-1024 — below the 2048 bits RFC 8301 recommends, and disallowed for new signatures by NIST SP 800-131A since 2014
weak_rotation: An RSA-1024 DKIM key is still published beside a 2048-bit one — retire it at the next key rotation
broken: DKIM key uses RSA under 1024 bits (broken)
unparseable: DKIM key found but could not be parsed
revoked: DKIM key explicitly revoked (p= empty) — deliberate operator action

present: BIMI brand indicator published (logo eligible to display)
dmarc_weak: BIMI logo published but DMARC is not at enforcement (p=quarantine or p=reject) — mailbox providers will not display the logo

chain_incomplete: DNSSEC key published but the chain does not validate (AD flag not set)

unsigned: The TLD is not DNSSEC signed, so this domain cannot enable DNSSEC

present: CAA records restrict certificate issuance (no iodef= reporting contact)

single: Only one authoritative nameserver (RFC 1034 calls for at least two)

some_lame: At least one nameserver listed at the parent registry is lame — it does not answer authoritatively for this zone (RFC 1034)

all_closed: Authoritative nameservers do not also serve open recursion (RFC 5358 / BCP 140)
some_open: At least one authoritative nameserver also serves open recursion — abusable for DNS amplification attacks (RFC 5358 / BCP 140)

present: IPv6 address published (routing could not be checked)
unrouted: IPv6 address published but not routed — unreachable from the internet

not-found: IPv4 (legacy IP) prefix has no Route Origin Authorization (RPKI)
invalid: IPv4 (legacy IP) route conflicts with its Route Origin Authorization (RPKI invalid)
lookup_failed: IPv4 (legacy IP) RPKI check could not run (RIPEstat lookup failed)

in_ris: IPv4 (legacy IP) route registered in IRR
not_in_ris: IPv4 (legacy IP) route not registered in IRR / RIS
lookup_failed: IPv4 (legacy IP) IRR/RIS check could not run (RIPEstat lookup failed)

not-found: IPv6 prefix has no Route Origin Authorization (RPKI)
invalid: IPv6 route conflicts with its Route Origin Authorization (RPKI invalid)
lookup_failed: IPv6 RPKI check could not run (RIPEstat lookup failed)

not_in_ris: IPv6 route not registered in IRR / RIS
lookup_failed: IPv6 IRR/RIS check could not run (RIPEstat lookup failed)

cert_expired: TLS certificate has expired — browsers block the site
cert_not_yet_valid: TLS certificate is not valid yet — browsers block the site
cert_self_signed: TLS certificate is self-signed — browsers block the site
cert_untrusted: TLS certificate does not chain to a trusted authority — browsers block the site
cert_error: TLS certificate failed verification — browsers block the site
no_tls: No HTTPS — the TLS connection failed

long_lived: TLS certificate lifetime exceeds 91 days — may indicate manual renewal

overdue: Certificate renewal overdue — under 10% of its lifetime left

no_match: TLS certificate does not cover this domain

missing_variant: Certificate does not cover the www / apex variant

complete: Server sends complete certificate chain (no AIA fallback needed)
incomplete: Server does not send its intermediate certificate (incomplete chain)

ok_preloaded: HSTS set with a long max-age and includeSubDomains; domain is preloaded
ok: HSTS set with a long max-age and includeSubDomains
weak_subdomains: HSTS is missing the includeSubDomains directive
weak_both: HSTS max-age is under 180 days and includeSubDomains is missing
missing: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) not set

pending: HSTS preload submission pending — accepted by hstspreload.org, waiting for the next Chrome release
preload_directive: HSTS preload directive present but the domain has not been submitted to hstspreload.org
not_preloaded: Domain is not on the HSTS preload list — a browser's first visit is not protected
not_ready: Not on the HSTS preload list; the HSTS header needs fixing first

M: SSL Labs grade: M (certificate name mismatch)
T: SSL Labs grade: T (certificate not trusted)

http1: HTTP/1.1 only — server does not support HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 (http1mustdie.com)

http_available: Port 80 serves content without redirecting to HTTPS

https_same_host: First redirect hop goes to HTTPS on same host
off_host_first: First redirect hop goes to a different host before HTTPS

unified: Apex and www variants unified (one redirects to the other)
canonical: Apex and www both serve the site, and both pages name the same one as canonical (rel=canonical)
split: Apex and www both serve content but neither redirects to the other (split-brain site)
half_missing: Only one of apex / www has DNS records — users typing the other form get a DNS error
half_missing_apex: Apex has no A/AAAA records — users typing the bare domain get a DNS error
half_missing_www: www variant has no A/AAAA records — users typing www get a DNS error

origin_no_version: Server header discloses software name (no version)

set: Clickjacking protection set (X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors)
missing: No clickjacking protection — neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors is set

weak: Referrer-Policy present but using a weak value

strict: CSP script-src is strict (nonce/hash, strict-dynamic, or 'none')
none: CSP script-src is strict (nonce/hash, strict-dynamic, or 'none')
nonce_or_hash: CSP script-src uses nonce/hash (strict-dynamic would be stronger)
host_allowlist: CSP script-src uses a host allowlist (weaker than nonce/hash)
wildcard_or_scheme: CSP script-src allows a wildcard or a whole scheme
report_only: CSP is only sent as Report-Only — nothing is enforced

set_dangerous: X-XSS-Protection is set to a filtering mode (deprecated; can introduce flaws)

all_secure: All cookies set the Secure flag
some_insecure: Some cookies are missing the Secure flag

missing_or_bad: Some cookies have no usable SameSite attribute

invalid_prefix: A cookie uses a __Host-/__Secure- prefix without meeting its rules

present_no_expiry: security.txt has no Expires: field (required by RFC 9116)

custom_404: Default error page customised (no server disclosure)
default_no_version: Default error page detected (server software disclosed, no version)
default_with_version: Default error page detected with version disclosure
spa_or_2xx: Default error page check did not run (probe returned 2xx/3xx — SPA shell, wildcard route, or WAF redirect)
error: Default error page check could not run (probe failed)

public_wildcard: CORS allows any origin without credentials (ACAO: *) — public responses only, no cookies sent
allow_listed: CORS allows a fixed origin and does not trust arbitrary ones
weak_wildcard_with_credentials: CORS — wildcard origin combined with credentials
weak_reflective: CORS — server reflects arbitrary Origin: header (any origin trusted)

in_sync: Server clock in sync with UTC
minor_skew: Server clock skew is small but noticeable
bad_skew: Server clock is more than 5 minutes off — can break HSTS, OAuth and certificate validation

all_external_have_sri: External scripts and stylesheets use Subresource Integrity
no_external_scripts: No external scripts or stylesheets that need Subresource Integrity
some_external_have_sri: Some external scripts or stylesheets have Subresource Integrity, but not all
external_without_sri: External scripts or stylesheets load without Subresource Integrity (SRI)

none: No mixed content in page body
passive_only: Passive mixed content present (images/media over HTTP)
active: Mixed content: scripts or styles loaded over HTTP on an HTTPS page

multiple: More than one SPF record published — receivers treat SPF as broken

clean: SPF record has no empty lookups or deprecated mechanisms
uses_ptr: SPF uses the deprecated ptr mechanism
too_many_void: SPF has more than two lookups that return nothing — receivers may treat it as broken
missing_include: SPF includes a domain with no SPF record — receivers treat SPF as broken

multiple: More than one DMARC record published — receivers ignore DMARC entirely

authorized: DMARC reports sent to other domains are authorized by them
unauthorized: DMARC reports go to a domain that has not authorized them — those reports are not sent

all: Every MX host has an address
some_missing: An MX host has no A or AAAA record — mail routed to it bounces

all_confirmed: Mail server addresses have reverse DNS that maps back to them
missing_or_mismatch: A mail server address has no reverse DNS, or it does not map back

published: Null MX published: the domain declares it receives no mail
missing: No MX records and no null MX — senders try to deliver to the domain's web address

all_covered: MTA-STS policy names every MX host
uncovered_testing: MTA-STS policy does not name every MX host — mail to them fails once enforced
uncovered_enforce: MTA-STS policy does not name every MX host — senders refuse to deliver to them

ok: MTA-STS policy is cached for a week or longer
short: MTA-STS policy max_age is under a week

none: No CNAME on the domain or its www form points at a missing name
dangling: A CNAME points at a name that no longer exists — subdomain takeover risk

modern: DNSSEC uses a current signing algorithm
not_recommended: DNSSEC signs with RSASHA512, which is not recommended for signing
deprecated: DNSSEC signs only with a forbidden algorithm (such as SHA-1) — validators treat the zone as unsigned

two_or_more: At least two nameservers reachable over IPv6
fewer_than_two: Fewer than two nameservers reachable over IPv6

diverse: Nameservers spread over more than one network
single_network: All nameservers checked are in one network

not-found: A nameserver route has no RPKI ROA — it can be hijacked
lookup_failed: Nameserver RPKI could not be checked

all: Every mail server checked is reachable over IPv6
partial: Some mail servers have no IPv6 address
none: No mail server has an IPv6 address

not-found: A mail server route has no RPKI ROA — it can be hijacked
invalid: A mail server route is RPKI-invalid
lookup_failed: Mail server RPKI could not be checked

unprobed: TLS 1.0 / 1.1 could not be tested from this system

required: Forward secrecy required for every connection
static_rsa: Static RSA key exchange accepted — those connections have no forward secrecy
null_cipher: NULL cipher accepted — traffic can be sent unencrypted
unprobed: Key exchange could not be tested from this system

strong: Certificate key and signature are strong
weak_key: Certificate key is too short (under 2048-bit RSA or 256-bit EC)
weak_signature: Certificate is signed with SHA-1 or MD5

legacy_path: security.txt is only at the legacy /security.txt path

match: security.txt Canonical lists where the file was found
mismatch: security.txt Canonical does not list where the file was found

none: No deprecated HPKP or Expect-CT headers
expect_ct: Expect-CT is set — deprecated and has no effect
hpkp: Public-Key-Pins (HPKP) is set — deprecated and risky

missing: Page does not declare its language (<html lang>)
